name: Gremlin
sum: Gremlin is a small leptoceratopsid from the Campanian Oldman Formation of Alberta, known from one frontal bone.
wsnote: Approximately 2 m long according to the authors (Carleton University news story, 2023; see sources).
holotype: TMP 2011.053.0027, an isolated right frontal bone — Oldman Formation, southern Alberta (about 77 Ma).
material: Holotype only; PBDB also records a Two Medicine Formation occurrence (a frontal described alongside).
biology: Small four-footed plant-eater that browsed low vegetation with a beak-like snout; lacked facial horns and had only a small frill (Carleton University news story).
author: Ryan et al. 2023

sources.text: Ryan, M. J., Micucci, L., Rizo, H., et al. 2023. A new Late Cretaceous leptoceratopsid (Dinosauria: Ceratopsia) from the Oldman Formation (Campanian) of Alberta, Canada. In: Windows into sauropsid and synapsid evolution: essays in honor of Louis L. Jacobs, pp. 151–165.
Carleton University, Department of Earth Sciences. 2023. New Late Cretaceous horned-dinosaur discovered in southern Alberta (news story, accessed 2026-11-23).
